name: Floe 1.1.0-alpha.8
body:
**Pre-alpha — for testing only.** Expect bugs.

Windows installers:
- `Floe_1.1.0-alpha.8_x64-setup.exe` — built-in engine (recommended).
- `Floe-polars_1.1.0-alpha.8_x64-setup.exe` — adds the native Polars engine (about 10 MB larger).

Builds are **not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen will show a warning. Choose *More info* then *Run anyway*. SHA-256 checksums are attached. There is no auto-update yet.

Linux packages (Debian and Ubuntu, 64-bit, built on Ubuntu 22.04):
- `Floe_1.1.0-alpha.8_amd64.deb` — built-in engine (recommended).
- `Floe-polars_1.1.0-alpha.8_amd64.deb` — adds the native Polars engine.

Both are the package `floe`, so installing one replaces the other. Install with `sudo apt install ./Floe_1.1.0-alpha.8_amd64.deb`; apt pulls in WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3.

## Linux packages: what was run

Each package was installed from the `.deb` into a clean Ubuntu container, started under WebDriver and driven through the same Tauri commands the app uses.

| Ubuntu | Display | Package | Result | Checks | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22.04 | Wayland (weston, headless) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |
| 22.04 | X11 (Xvfb) | builtin | passed | 13 of 13 |  |
| 22.04 | X11 (Xvfb) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |
| 24.04 | Wayland (weston, headless) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |
| 24.04 | X11 (Xvfb) | builtin | passed | 13 of 13 |  |
| 24.04 | X11 (Xvfb) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |
| 26.04 | Wayland (weston, headless) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |
| 26.04 | X11 (Xvfb) | builtin | passed | 13 of 13 |  |
| 26.04 | X11 (Xvfb) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |
| 26.10 | Wayland (weston, headless) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |
| 26.10 | X11 (Xvfb) | builtin | passed | 13 of 13 |  |
| 26.10 | X11 (Xvfb) | polars | passed | 15 of 15 |  |

### What this does not show

- The packages are built on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35). Releases older than that are not covered, and nothing was built for arm64, Fedora, Arch or as an AppImage or RPM.
- Containers have no GPU, so WebKitGTK runs with software rendering and its web process sandbox switched off. Hardware acceleration, NVIDIA drivers, HiDPI and fractional scaling were not exercised.
- Wayland is a headless weston compositor, not GNOME. Nothing was tested inside a real GNOME, KDE or other desktop session, with its file chooser portal, drag and drop from a file manager, double-clicking a `.floe` file, input methods, themes or printing.
- Only the checks listed in the Detail column and in `checks.json` ran. A pass means the app starts, its Tauri bridge answers, the Polars package runs one CSV plan end to end and the built-in engine runs the sample project; it says nothing about the rest of the interface.
- Ubuntu 26.10 appears as not tested whenever Docker Hub has no `ubuntu:26.10` image or its WebKitGTK packages could not be installed.

Floe runs entirely on your PC. Files are never uploaded.

name: Floe 1.1.0-alpha.4
body:
## What's new

**Polars engine upgraded from 0.46 to 0.55.2** (the `Floe-polars` installer). Everything the Polars engine runs was re-checked against the built-in engine: 27 shared test queries, 354 column-profile and distinct-value checks, grid pages and CSV / Parquet / Arrow / Excel exports all match. The web app and the built-in `Floe` installer do not use Polars and are unchanged.

**Results now match the built-in engine more closely**
- `Number.Round` rounds half to even, like Power Query (2.5 gives 2, 3.5 gives 4). Polars used to round half away from zero, so the two engines disagreed.
- Whole-number conversions, the Round numbers step and date differences round half up like the built-in engine (for example -2.5 gives -2). Polars used to give -3.
- Distinct values in the column filter list show failed conversions as their own "Error" entry instead of merging them with blanks.

**Installer size:** the Polars installer grows from 6.2 MB to 8.9 MB with the newer Polars. The built-in installer stays at 2.2 MB.

**Also in this build:** everything from alpha.3 (custom dropdowns, number steppers, tooltips, context menus, step reordering and the filter popover fix).

**Known difference (unchanged):** with Polars, text sorts in plain character order, and so do the minimum and maximum shown for text columns in the profile. The built-in engine uses natural, accent-insensitive order.

---

**Pre-alpha — for testing only.** The Rust shell and the Polars engine were only recently compiled for the first time: expect bugs.

Windows installers:
- `Floe_1.1.0-alpha.4_x64-setup.exe` — built-in engine (recommended).
- `Floe-polars_1.1.0-alpha.4_x64-setup.exe` — adds the native Polars engine (about 30 MB larger).

Builds are **not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen will show a warning. Choose *More info* then *Run anyway*. SHA-256 checksums are attached. There is no auto-update yet.

Floe runs entirely on your PC. Files are never uploaded.

name: Floe 1.1.0-alpha.3
body:
## What's new

**Every browser-native control is gone.** Everything you click, type into or open is now drawn and controlled by Floe's own CSS, so the app looks and behaves the same on every platform.

- **Dropdowns** are custom: full keyboard control, type-ahead, a check mark on the current choice, column type chips, and a built-in search box on long column lists.
- **Number fields** are custom steppers: arrow keys and +/- buttons, and anything that isn't a number is filtered out as you type.
- **Tooltips** are custom and also appear when you tab to a control with the keyboard.
- **Right-click** no longer opens the browser menu: text fields get Cut / Copy / Paste / Select all, and selected text gets Copy.
- **Checkboxes, scrollbars (including Firefox) and the textarea resize handle** are styled by the app.
- **Reordering steps** uses a custom drag with a ghost and a drop line instead of the browser's drag image. Esc cancels the drag.

**Fixes and polish**
- Dialogs keep Tab focus inside them and focus the first visible field when they open.
- Delete, ?, Ctrl+Z and paste no longer fire while a dropdown has focus.
- The right-click menu now appears above the command palette.
- The column filter popover and Copy column show the error instead of hanging on "Loading…" when a result has expired.
- Grid text is now vertically centred in its row (row density is unchanged).
- Code comments were removed from the app source, and the automated UI test now checks every step dialog for native controls and exercises dropdowns, steppers, tooltips and step reordering.

**Not covered:** operating-system file pickers and the browser's "unsaved changes" prompt when closing a tab are controlled by the OS or browser and can't be restyled.

---

**Pre-alpha — for testing only.** The Rust shell and the Polars engine were only recently compiled for the first time: expect bugs.

Windows installers:
- `Floe_1.1.0-alpha.3_x64-setup.exe` — built-in engine (recommended).
- `Floe-polars_1.1.0-alpha.3_x64-setup.exe` — adds the native Polars engine (about 30 MB larger).

Builds are **not code-signed**, so Windows SmartScreen will show a warning. Choose *More info* then *Run anyway*. SHA-256 checksums are attached. There is no auto-update yet.
